title: Cyclic Fueter Theory: Lean 4 Formalization of Selected Results
description:
This software repository contains Lean 4 source files developed in connection with the Cyclic Fueter Theory (CFT) research program. It formalizes selected algebraic and geometric statements involving quaternionic algebra, Fueter-type operators, matrix and spinor constructions, quantum-geometric identities, Cartan-frame calculations, the reduced Einstein–Yang–Mills action and its four-dimensional field equations, distributional junction conditions, characteristic evolution and constraint propagation, zero-mode calculations, and consequences of the action principle for the Einstein–Yang–Mills dumbbell (caps as closed radiation universes, the AdS₂ × S² neck, JT/Schwarzian reduction, thermodynamics, stability, the shape and junction of the dumbbell, a reduced action with canonical constraints and a Wheeler–DeWitt equation for the spherically symmetric sector, and a two-dimensional Dirac field).

Version 1.2.0 contains 2743 declarations (2740 theorems and 3 private lemmas) in 261 modules, with no sorry and no project-specific axioms, plus 556 index aliases. New in this version: local uniqueness, continuous dependence and local existence (by the Banach fixed-point theorem) for the wedge characteristic initial-value problem of the spherically symmetric Einstein–Yang–Mills system, for characteristic data C¹ on ℝ, with r and Ω bounded below by a positive constant (evolution equations only; the constraints and the version including the cap centre r = 0 remain open); classical field equations written through Fueter-type operators (Maxwell's equations as one biquaternionic Fueter equation, linearised gravity and the Newtonian limit, the second and contracted Bianchi identities, mechanics, continuum laws and special relativity, quaternionic Kepler and rigid-body mechanics); and the nonlinear Einstein equations from the first-order Cartan–Palatini action, with torsion-freeness from the connection variation, Lorentz signature, gauge covariance of the curvature, and the correspondence between frame and coordinate Einstein tensors. Earlier versions are described in docs/ZENODO_DESCRIPTION_v1.1.1.md and before; the full description of this version is docs/ZENODO_DESCRIPTION_v1.2.0.md. The additions were not audited by an independent reviewer. Lean verifies each theorem from its declared assumptions and imported results. Formalization does not by itself establish that a physical model, external theorem, or interpretation is appropriate.

The project targets Lean 4.15.0 and Mathlib v4.15.0. To reproduce the build, install Elan and run `lake update`, `lake exe cache get`, and `lake build` from the repository root.
